LO-2.learner_does: divides a whole number of up to four digits by 100 by shifting every digit two places to the right, producing the correct quotient

LO-3.learner_does: explains why the place-value shift is the reliable rule and the crossed-off zero is not

LO-3.narration_text: Explain why the place-value shift is the reliable rule for dividing by 10 or 100.

scenes.narration_text: Today we are looking at what happens to a whole number when you divide it by 10, and then by 100.
scenes.visual_description: a teacher standing in front of a clean, empty whiteboard

source_refs.quote: Today we are looking at what happens to a whole number when you divide it by 10, and then by 100.

scenes.narration_text: Every whole number is built out of place value columns. From the right, we have ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.
scenes.visual_description: a diagram of place value columns

source_refs.quote: Every whole number is built out of place value columns. From the right, we have ones, then tens, then hundreds, then thousands.

scenes.narration_text: Dividing by 10 makes a number ten times smaller.
scenes.visual_description: a number being divided by 10, with the digits shifting one place to the right
scenes.media_rationale: the learner must see the digits shifting

source_refs.quote: Dividing by 10 makes a number ten times smaller.

scenes.narration_text: When a number gets ten times smaller, every digit in it moves one place to the right. The thousands digit becomes the hundreds digit. The hundreds digit becomes the tens digit. The tens digit becomes the ones digit.
scenes.visual_description: a number being divided by 10, with the digits shifting one place to the right
scenes.media_rationale: the learner must see the digits shifting

source_refs.quote: When a number gets ten times smaller, every digit in it moves one place to the right. The thousands digit becomes the hundreds digit. The hundreds digit becomes the tens digit. The tens digit becomes the ones digit.

scenes.narration_text: Dividing by 100 makes a number one hundred times smaller.
scenes.visual_description: a number being divided by 100, with the digits shifting two places to the right
scenes.media_rationale: the learner must see the digits shifting

source_refs.quote: Dividing by 100 makes a number one hundred times smaller.

scenes.narration_text: One hundred is ten times ten. So dividing by 100 is the same as dividing by 10, and then dividing by 10 again.
scenes.visual_description: a number being divided by 100, with the digits shifting two places to the right
scenes.media_rationale: the learner must see the digits shifting

source_refs.quote: One hundred is ten times ten. So dividing by 100 is the same as dividing by 10, and then dividing by 10 again.

scenes.narration_text: It helps to know why this works rather than only that it works.

source_refs.quote: It helps to know why this works rather than only that it works.

scenes.narration_text: A digit in the tens column is worth ten times what the same digit is worth in the ones column. So moving a digit one column to the right divides what it is worth by exactly ten. Doing that to every digit at once divides the whole number by ten.
scenes.visual_description: a diagram of place value columns

source_refs.quote: A digit in the tens column is worth ten times what the same digit is worth in the ones column. So moving a digit one column to the right divides what it is worth by exactly ten. Doing that to every digit at once divides the whole number by ten.

scenes.narration_text: People often say 'dividing by 10 means crossing off a zero.' That works for whole numbers that end in a zero and it fails for every other number, because there is no zero to cross off.

source_refs.quote: People often say 'dividing by 10 means crossing off a zero.' That works for whole numbers that end in a zero and it fails for every other number, because there is no zero to cross off.

scenes.narration_text: The reliable version is the one about columns: every digit shifts one place right for each ten you divide by.
scenes.visual_description: a diagram of place value columns

source_refs.quote: The reliable version is the one about columns: every digit shifts one place right for each ten you divide by.

scenes.narration_text: Summary: divide by 10, every digit moves one column to the right. Divide by 100, every digit moves two columns to the right. The digits stay in the same order and keep their own identities throughout.

source_refs.quote: Summary: divide by 10, every digit moves one column to the right. Divide by 100, every digit moves two columns to the right. The digits stay in the same order and keep their own identities throughout.

span.quote: That is the whole rule. It is not a trick about zeros. The zeros only look like they are being removed because the ones column has nowhere further right to go.

design_notes: The lesson starts with an introduction to the topic, followed by an explanation of the place-value shift. The learner is then guided through the process of dividing by 10 and 100, with a focus on the reliable rule. The lesson concludes with a summary and a chance for the learner to practice what they have learned.
